speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if your tremors are present at rest or only when you are performing voluntary movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the description of a unilateral resting tremor that has progressed to affect fine motor skills is very concerning. To further differentiate potential causes, have you noticed any stiffness in his limbs or a "shuffling" gait when he walks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That constellation of a unilateral resting tremor, bradykinesia (soft speech, reduced facial expressions), and cognitive decline is highly suggestive of Parkinson's disease with dementia. Given his age and recent memory issues, we must rule out other etiologies before confirming.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain showing atrophy patterns or white matter changes.
